text:
mia: Heads-up — after installing redwoodctl via Homebrew on a shared mac, `redwoodctl login` finishes in browser but CLI keeps prompting for device code. localserve ends up using a different profile. Anyone seen this?

lee: probably a permissions issue on ~/.config/redwood. Can you run `stat ~/.config/redwood` and `cat ~/.config/redwood/config.yaml`?

mia: stat shows OWNER=root, GROUP=wheel, perms 700. config.yaml is readable but auth.cache exists and is not writable by my user. I think the brew install used sudo earlier.

randall: yep. If the CLI can't write the token cache it can't renew tokens and will request auth again. localserve falls back to system profile detection which can pick a different profile when user config is inaccessible.

mia: what's the safest fix? I'd rather not wipe anything in case other users rely on it.

lee: safest: `sudo chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) ~/.config/redwood` — that transfers ownership to your user. If you need multi-user sharing, we should adjust perms or move to a global config path, but that's more work.

mia: did the chown, retried login, works now. localserve sees my profile. Thanks.

randall: action items: we should (1) update the Homebrew postinstall to not create root-owned files or to use the installing user, (2) add a preflight in redwoodctl that detects unwritable config dir and prints a clear error suggesting `chown`, (3) update quickstart docs to warn about running installers as root.

devex-bot: Created issue #4598: "installer: avoid creating root-owned ~/.config/redwood during Homebrew postinstall" and linked PR draft.

mia: marking this resolved for onboarding. I can paste exact install commands I ran if useful for reproducing in CI images.

lee: please paste them in #devex later. CI images that pipe installs as root then switch users may hit this; we should add an e2e test in the brew formula job. :thumbsup:
